title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 49 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 371–378 (Night 49, continuing directly from nights-48), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 49 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. In the Christian girl's palace Prince Sharkān drinks, listens to her singers and trades verse with her, plays chess and loses, and spends two more days as her guest. Then armed patriarchs burst in, naming him as Sharkān son of ʿUmar and demanding him as their king's prize; the girl swears by the Messiah that he is her guest, refuses to betray him, and proposes that the patriarchs meet him one at a time. The night breaks off as Shahrazad perceives the morning. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَالْأَرْبَعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿatu wa-al-arbaʿūn
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the ninth and the forty,
sentences.i: And when it was the forty-ninth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ مَازَالَتْ تَشْرَبُ وَتَسْقِي شَرْكَانَ إِلَى أَنْ غَابَ عَنْ رُشْدِهِ مِنَ الشَّرَابِ وَمِنْ سُكْرِ مَحَبَّتِهَا
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-jāriyata mā zālat tashrabu wa-tasqī Sharkāna ilā an ghāba ʿan rushdihi mina al-sharābi wa-min sukri maḥabbatihā
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy, that the girl did not cease drinking and giving-to-drink Sharkān, until he was absent from his right-mind from the drink and from the drunkenness of her love.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the girl went on drinking and pouring for Sharkān until he lost his wits, from the wine and from the intoxication of loving her.
sentences.n: مَازَالَتْ is printed as one word (mā zālat, "did not cease"); it takes the following present verbs to mean "kept on drinking and pouring". غَابَ عَنْ رُشْدِهِ, literally "was absent from his sound judgement", is the idiom for losing one's wits.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا قَالَتْ لِلْجَارِيَةِ يَا مَرْجَانَةُ هَاتِي لَنَا شَيْئًا مِنْ آلَةِ الطَّرَبِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā qālat li-al-jāriyati yā Marjānatu hātī lanā shayʾan min ālati al-ṭarabi
sentences.l: Then that she said to the girl: O Marjāna, bring to-us something from the instrument of mirth.
sentences.i: Then she said to the maid, "Marjāna, bring us some instrument of music."
sentences.n: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا is a stock narrative opener, "then she". The speaker is Abrīza and the "girl" is her maid Marjāna. آلَةُ الطَّرَبِ, literally "the instrument of delight", is a musical instrument. The printed آ is kept as in the edition.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً وَغَابَتْ لَحْظَةً وَأَتَتْ بِعُودٍ جَلْقِيٍّ وَجَنْكٍ عَجَمِيٍّ وَنَايٍ تَنْرِيٍّ وَقَانُونٍ مِصْرِيٍّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan wa-ghābat laḥẓatan wa-atat bi-ʿūdin jalqiyyin wa-jankin ʿajamiyyin wa-nāyin tanriyyin wa-qānūnin miṣriyyin
sentences.l: And she said: Hearing and obedience; and she was absent a moment, and she came with a lute, Jillīqī, and a harp, Persian, and a flute, tanrī, and a zither, Egyptian.
sentences.i: She said, "With hearing and obedience," and was gone for a moment. Then she came back with a Damascene lute, a Persian harp, a tanrī flute and an Egyptian zither.
sentences.n: سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً is the servant's stock reply, "(I give) hearing and obedience", an accusative of the thing offered. جَلْقِيّ (from Jillīq, a poetic name for Damascus) and the other adjectives name where each instrument comes from. جَنْك is the Persian harp (chang). تَنْرِيّ is obscure to us and may be corrupt; we point it as printed and leave it untranslated. قَانُون is the plucked zither.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ الْعُودَ وَأَصْلَحَتْهُ وَشَدَّتْهُ وَغَنَّتْ عَلَيْهِ بِصَوْتٍ رَخِيمٍ أَرَقَّ مِنَ النَّسِيمِ وَأَعْذَبَ مِنْ مَاءِ التَّسْنِيمِ مِنْ قَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhati al-jāriyatu al-ʿūda wa-aṣlaḥat-hu wa-shaddat-hu wa-ghannat ʿalayhi bi-ṣawtin rakhīmin araqqa mina al-nasīmi wa-aʿdhaba min māʾi al-tasnīmi min qalbin salīmin wa-anshadat taqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And the girl took the lute and set it right and tightened it and sang upon it with a voice, soft, more delicate than the breeze and sweeter than the water of Tasnīm, from a heart, sound; and she recited, saying these verses:
sentences.i: The girl took the lute, tuned it and tightened its strings, and sang to it in a soft voice, gentler than the breeze and sweeter than the water of Tasnīm, out of a sound heart. Then she recited these verses.
sentences.n: التَّسْنِيم is the name of a spring in Paradise, so "the water of Tasnīm" is a figure for the sweetest drink imaginable. قَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ, "a sound heart", is a heart free of malice. أَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ, "she recited, saying", is the usual way of introducing verse.

sentences.t:
عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْ عَيْنَيْكَ كَمْ سَفَكَتْ دَمَاً * وَكَمْ فَوَّقَتْ مِنْكَ اللَّوَاحِظُ اَسْهُمَاً
اُجِلُّ حَبِيبَاً جَائِرَاً فِي حَبِيبِهِ * حَرَامٌ عَلَيْهِ اَنْ يَرِقَّ وَيَرْحَمَا
هَنِيئَاً لِطَرْفٍ بَاتَ فِيكَ مُسَهَّدَاً * وَطُوبَى لِقَلْبٍ ظَلَّ فِيكَ مُتَيَّمَاً
تَحَكَّمْتَ فِي قَتْلِي فَاِنَّكَ مَالِكِي * بِرُوحِي اَفْدِي الْحَاكِمَ الْمُتَحَكِّمَا
sentences.tr:
ʿafā Allāhu ʿan ʿaynayka kam safakat damāan * wa-kam fawwaqat minka al-lawāḥiẓu ashumāan
ujillu ḥabīban jāʾiran fī ḥabībihi * ḥarāmun ʿalayhi an yariqqa wa-yarḥamā
hanīʾan li-ṭarfin bāta fīka musahhadan * wa-ṭūbā li-qalbin ẓalla fīka mutayyaman
taḥakkamta fī qatlī fa-innaka mālikī * bi-rūḥī afdī al-ḥākima al-mutaḥakkimā
sentences.l:
God pardon your two eyes: how much blood they have shed * and how many arrows have the glances notched from you!
I hold in awe a beloved, unjust toward his lover: * forbidden to him that he be tender and show mercy.
Happy be an eye that spent the night in you sleepless, * and bliss to a heart that stayed in you enslaved.
You have taken sway over my killing, for you are my owner: * with my soul I ransom the ruler, the despot.
sentences.i: God forgive your eyes, for how much blood they have spilled, and how many arrows your glances have notched against me! I revere a beloved who wrongs his lover, for it is forbidden him to soften and show mercy. Happy the eye that lay sleepless for you, and blessed the heart that stayed bewitched by you. You have taken command of my death, for you are my master; I would ransom with my soul this ruler, this tyrant.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the edition prints it, vowel marks and all, including the bare alif carrying a mark in اُجِلُّ, اَسْهُمَاً and اَنْ, and the tanwīn written after the alif in دَمَاً, حَبِيبَاً and the like. فَوَّقَ السَّهْمَ is "to set the arrow's notch on the string", so the glances are archers and the lover's heart the target. The second line is a lover's paradox: it is the beloved's right to be cruel, so mercy would be forbidden to him. The fourth line puns on the ruling root ح-ك-م: تَحَكَّمْتَ, الْحَاكِمَ, الْمُتَحَكِّمَا.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَتْ كُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنَ الْجَوَارِي وَمَعَهَا آلَتُهَا تُنْشِدُ عَلَيْهَا أَبْيَاتًا بِلِسَانِ الرُّومِيَّةِ فَطَرِبَ شَرْكَانُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāmat kullu wāḥidatin mina al-jawārī wa-maʿahā ālatuhā tunshidu ʿalayhā abyātan bi-lisāni al-rūmiyyati fa-ṭariba Sharkānu
sentences.l: Then rose every one of the girls, and with her her instrument, reciting upon it verses in the tongue of the Greek; and Sharkān was moved with delight.
sentences.i: Then each of the girls rose, her instrument beside her, and chanted verses to it in the Greek tongue, and Sharkān was stirred to rapture.
sentences.n: الرُّومِيَّةِ is the feminine adjective "Rūmī" (Byzantine, Greek-speaking Christian) used as a noun for the language, "the Rūmī (tongue)". طَرِبَ is to be moved to delight, especially by music.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ غَنَّتِ الْجَارِيَةُ سَيِّدَتُهُنَّ أَيْضًا وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا مُسْلِمُ أَمَا فَهِمْتَ مَا أَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma ghannati al-jāriyatu sayyidatuhunna ayḍan wa-qālat lahu yā muslimu amā fahimta mā aqūlu
sentences.l: Then sang the girl, their mistress, also, and she said to him: O Muslim, have you not understood what I say?
sentences.i: Then the girl, their mistress, sang as well, and said to him, "O Muslim, have you not understood what I am saying?"
sentences.n: سَيِّدَتُهُنَّ, "their mistress", stands beside الْجَارِيَةُ as an apposition: the girl who is their lady. يَا مُسْلِمُ, "O Muslim", is how she addresses Sharkān, whom she takes for a Muslim.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَا وَلَكِنْ مَا طَرِبْتُ إِلَّا عَلَى حُسْنِ أَنَا مَلِكٌ
sentences.tr: qāla lā wa-lākin mā ṭaribtu illā ʿalā ḥusni anā malikun
sentences.l: He said: No; but I was not moved-to-delight except upon the beauty-of I [am] a king.
sentences.i: He said, "No; but I was moved only by the beauty of your fingertips."
sentences.n: The last words, حُسْنِ أَنَا مَلِكٌ, make poor sense as printed ("the beauty of — I am a king"). They may be a corrupt or run-together form of حُسْنِ أَنَامِلِكِ, "the beauty of your fingertips" (the letters are the same apart from the space), which suits a lute-player; that is only a conjecture, so the words are pointed as printed and the idiomatic line is our guess. Note also that ما … إلا is the usual "only" construction.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَتْ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنْ غَنَّيْتُ لَكَ بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ مَاذَا تَصْنَعُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥikat wa-qālat lahu in ghannaytu laka bi-al-ʿarabiyyati mādhā taṣnaʿu
sentences.l: And she laughed, and said to him: If I sing to you in the Arabic, what will you do?
sentences.i: She laughed and said to him, "If I sing to you in Arabic, what will you do?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ مَا كُنْتُ أَمْلِكُ عَقْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla mā kuntu amliku ʿaqlī
sentences.l: And he said: I would not be possessing my mind.
sentences.i: He said, "I would not be master of my wits."
sentences.n: مَا كُنْتُ أَمْلِكُ is a past-continuous negative, "I was not possessing", used here for the conditional result: "I should not be in command of my mind".

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْ آلَةَ الطَّرَبِ فَغَيَّرَتِ الضَّرْبَ وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhat ālata al-ṭarabi fa-ghayyarati al-ḍarba wa-anshadat taqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: And she took the instrument of delight and changed the striking, and recited, saying poetry:
sentences.i: She took up the instrument of delight, changed the mode of her playing, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: الضَّرْبَ is the striking of the strings, that is, the mode or measure of playing; changing it marks the shift to Arabic song.

sentences.t:
طَعْمُ التَّفَرُّقِ مُرُّ * فَهَلْ لِذَلِكَ صَبْرُ
تَعَرَّضَتْ لِي ثَلْثُ * صَدُّو بُعْدُ وَهَجْرُ
اَهْوَى ظَرِيفَاً سَبَانِي * بِالْحُسْنِ وَالْهَجْرُ مُرُّ
sentences.tr:
ṭaʿmu al-tafarruqi murru * fa-hal li-dhālika ṣabru
taʿarraḍat lī thaltu * ṣaddū buʿdu wa-hajru
ahwā ẓarīfan sabānī * bi-al-ḥusni wa-al-hajru murru
sentences.l:
The taste of parting is bitter * so is there for that any patience?
There confronted me three * turning-away, distance, and desertion.
I love a charming one who captivated me * with beauty, and desertion is bitter.
sentences.i: The taste of parting is bitter; has anyone patience for that? Three things have come upon me: rebuff, distance and abandonment. I love a graceful one who has captured me with beauty, and being forsaken is bitter.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the edition prints it, vowel marks and all. Two forms are odd: ثَلْثُ is a short, sukūn form of ثَلَاثٌ ("three", read thalāth), and صَدُّو has a long final vowel for صَدٌّ ("turning away"), perhaps for the rhyme; so the three troubles are ṣadd, buʿd and hajr. The marks on the last line (وَالْهَجْرُ مُرُّ) give a rhyme in -ru throughout, which is why the case endings are as they are.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا نَظَرَتْ إِلَى شَرْكَانَ فَوَجَدَتْ شَرْكَانَ غَابَ عَنْ وُجُودِهِ وَصَارَ مَطْرُوحًا بَيْنَهُنَّ مَمْدُودًا سَاعَةً ثُمَّ أَفَاقَ وَتَذَكَّرَ الْغِنَاءَ قَالَ طَرَبًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā naẓarat ilā Sharkāna fa-wajadat Sharkāna ghāba ʿan wujūdihi wa-ṣāra maṭrūḥan baynahunna mamdūdan sāʿatan thumma afāqa wa-tadhakkara al-ghināʾa qāla ṭaraban
sentences.l: And when she finished with her poem, she looked at Sharkān and found Sharkān gone from his being, and he had become cast down among them, stretched out, an hour; then he recovered and remembered the singing; he said: delight.
sentences.i: When she had finished her poem she looked at Sharkān and found him lost to himself; he lay flung down among them, stretched out for an hour. Then he came to, remembered the singing, and said that he had been overcome by delight.
sentences.n: غَابَ عَنْ وُجُودِهِ, "gone from his own being", is the Sufi-flavoured phrase for being rapt out of oneself by music. The last two words, قَالَ طَرَبًا, are abrupt as printed ("he said: delight"); we take طَرَبًا as an accusative of cause ("from delight") or the content of what he said, and the idiomatic line follows that reading. وَجَدَتْ شَرْكَانَ غَابَ has no أَنَّ, the object followed directly by its predicate verb.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَا عَلَى الشَّرَابِ وَلَمْ يَزَالَا فِي لَعِبٍ وَلَهْوٍ إِىٰ أَنْ وَلَّى النَّهَارُ بِالرَّوَاحِ وَأَرْخَى اللَّيْلُ الْجَنَاحَ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbalā ʿalā al-sharābi wa-lam yazālā fī laʿibin wa-lahwin ilā an wallā al-nahāru bi-al-rawāḥi wa-arkhā al-laylu al-janāḥa
sentences.l: Then the two of them turned-to the drink, and did not cease in play and sport until the day turned-away with the going-out, and the night let-down the wing.
sentences.i: Then the two of them turned to the wine and kept on in play and sport until day withdrew with the evening's going and night lowered its wing.
sentences.n: إِىٰ is printed اى for إِلَى "to, until", with the lam missing; the sense is clear from the following أَنْ ("until"), and we point it with a dagger alif as the pronunciation ilā. أَقْبَلَا is dual, "the two of them", though only one companion has been named; read it as Sharkān and the girl. الرَّوَاحِ is the going-out or travel of the evening, and أَرْخَى اللَّيْلُ الْجَنَاحَ is the common figure of night spreading its wing over the world.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتْ إِىٰ مَرْقَدِهَا فَسَأَلَ شَرْكَانُ عَنْهَا فَقَالُوا لَهُ إِنَّهَا مَضَتْ إِلَى مَرْقَدِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāmat ilā marqadihā fa-saʾala Sharkānu ʿanhā fa-qālū lahu innahā maḍat ilā marqadihā
sentences.l: And she rose to her place-of-lying, and Sharkān asked about her, and they said to him: She has gone to her place-of-lying.
sentences.i: She rose and went to her bedchamber. Sharkān asked after her, and they told him, "She has gone to her bedchamber."
sentences.n: إِىٰ is printed اى again for إِلَى, with the lam missing, as above. مَرْقَد, from رَقَدَ "to lie down, sleep", is the place of sleeping, a bedchamber.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فِي وَدَاعَةِ اللَّهِ وَحِفْظِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla fī wadāʿati Allāhi wa-ḥifẓihi
sentences.l: And he said: In the repose-of God and His keeping.
sentences.i: He said, "May she rest in God's care and keeping."
sentences.n: فِي وَدَاعَةِ اللَّهِ is the farewell formula "in God's safe keeping"; the idiomatic line supplies the wish that is understood.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ سَيِّدَتِي تَدْعُوكَ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu aqbalat ʿalayhi al-jāriyatu wa-qālat lahu inna sayyidatī tadʿūka ilayhā
sentences.l: And when the morning became morning, the girl came toward him and said to him: Indeed my lady is calling you to her.
sentences.i: At daybreak the girl came to him and said, "My lady is calling you to her."

sentences.t: فَقَامَ مَعَهَا وَسَارَ خَلْفَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma maʿahā wa-sāra khalfahā
sentences.l: And he arose with her and went behind her.
sentences.i: So he rose and went with her, following behind.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرُبَ مِنْ مَكَانِهَا زَفَّتْهُ الْجَوَارِي بِالدُّفُوفِ وَالْمَوَاصِلِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى بَابٍ كَبِيرٍ وَهُوَ مِنَ الْعَاجِ مُرَصَّعٌ بِالدُّرَرِ وَالْجَوَاهِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaruba min makānihā zaffat-hu al-jawārī bi-al-dufūfi wa-al-mawāṣili ilā an waṣala ilā bābin kabīrin wa-huwa mina al-ʿājī murassaʿun bi-al-durari wa-al-jawāhiri
sentences.l: And when he drew near from her place, the girls bore-him-in-procession with the tambourines and the mawāṣil, until he arrived at a gate, large, and it was of the ivory, studded with the pearls and the jewels.
sentences.i: When he drew near her dwelling, the girls led him on in procession with tambourines and the mawāṣil, until he came to a great gate of ivory, studded with pearls and jewels.
sentences.n: الْمَوَاصِل is obscure; it seems to be a kind of instrument played with the tambourines (perhaps a slip for الْمَزَامِير, "pipes"), so it is left untranslated. زَفَّتْهُ is the verb used of leading a bride to her husband, here for the prince's ceremonial welcome. مُرَصَّعٌ is printed after وَهُوَ مِنَ الْعَاجِ and agrees with the gate.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلُوا مِنْهُ فَوَجَدُوا دَٰرًا كَبِيرَةً أَيْضًا وَفِي صَدْرِهَا إِيوَانٌ كَبِيرٌ مَفْرُوشٌ بِأَنْوَاعِ الْحَرِيرِ وَبِدَائِرِ ذَلِكَ الْإِيوَانِ شُبَّا بِيكُ مُفَتَّحَةٌ مُطِلَّةٌ عَلَى أَشْجَارٍ وَأَنْهَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalū minhu fa-wajadū dāran kabīratan ayḍan wa-fī ṣadrihā īwānun kabīrun mafrūshun bi-anwāʿi al-ḥarīri wa-bi-dāʾiri dhālika al-īwāni shubbā bīku mufattaḥatun muṭillatun ʿalā ashjārin wa-anhārin
sentences.l: And they entered from it and found a house, large, also; and in its chest a hall, large, spread with kinds of the silk; and around that hall windows, opened, overlooking trees and rivers.
sentences.i: They went in through it and found another great house, and at its head a great hall spread with every kind of silk. Round that hall were open windows overlooking trees and streams.
sentences.n: دَٰرًا is printed درا with the alif of دَارًا omitted, so it carries a dagger alif. شُبَّا بِيكُ is one word (شُبَّابِيك, "windows") split in the print; it is kept as printed. بِدَائِرِ ذَلِكَ الْإِيوَانِ is "around that hall".

sentences.t: وَفِى الْبَيْتِ صُوَرٌ مُجَسَّمَةٌ يَدْخُلُ فِيهَا الْهَوَاءُ فَتَتَحَرَّكُ فِي جَوْفِهَا آلَاتٌ فَيَتَخَيَّلُ لِلنَّاظِرِ أَنَّهَا تَتَكَلَّمُ
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-bayti ṣuwarun mujassamatun yadkhulu fīhā al-hawāʾu fa-tataḥarraku fī jawfihā ālātun fa-yatakhayyalu li-al-nāẓiri annahā tatakallamu
sentences.l: And in the house, figures, embodied; the air enters in them, and there move in their belly devices, and it appears-in-the-mind to the looker that they speak.
sentences.i: In the house stood solid figures; the air entered them and set machines moving inside, so that the onlooker imagined they were speaking.
sentences.n: The figures are automata worked by air passing through them. وَفِى is printed with ى.

sentences.t: وَالْجَارِيَةُ جَالِسَةٌ تَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-al-jāriyatu jālisatun tanẓuru ilayhim
sentences.l: And the girl was sitting, looking at them.
sentences.i: The girl sat looking at them.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتْهُ الْجَارِيَةُ نَهَضَتْ قَائِمَةً إِلَيْهِ وَمَسَكَتْ يَدَهُ وَأَجْلَسَتْهُ بِجَانِبِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarat-hu al-jāriyatu nahaḍat qāʾimatan ilayhi wa-masakat yadahu wa-ajlasat-hu bi-jānibihā
sentences.l: And when the girl saw him, she rose, standing to him, and took his hand and sat him by her side.
sentences.i: When the girl saw him she sprang up and stood before him, took his hand, and seated him at her side.
sentences.n: نَظَرَتْهُ uses نَظَرَ with a direct object ("looked at him"), and مَسَكَتْ is the colloquial verb for "took hold of"; both are Middle Arabic and are pointed as printed.

sentences.t: وَسَأَلَتْهُ عَنْ مَبِيتِهِ فَدَعَا لَهَا ثُمَّ جَلَسَا يَتَحَدَّثَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-saʾalat-hu ʿan mabītihi fa-daʿā lahā thumma jalasā yataḥaddathāni
sentences.l: And she asked him about his night-lodging, and he prayed for her, then the two sat conversing.
sentences.i: She asked him how he had passed the night; he prayed for her, and then the two sat talking together.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ أَتَعْرِفُ شَيْأً مِمَّا يَتَعَلَّقُ بِالْعَاشِقِينَ وَالْمُتَيَّمِينَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu a-taʿrifu shayʾan mimmā yataʿallaqu bi-al-ʿāshiqīna wa-al-mutayyamīna
sentences.l: Then she said to him: Do you know anything of what pertains to the lovers and the love-enslaved?
sentences.i: Then she said to him, "Do you know anything of what concerns lovers and those enslaved by love?"
sentences.n: مِمَّا is مِنْ + مَا, "of what". يَتَعَلَّقُ بِ is "to be connected with".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نَعَمْ أَعْرِفُ شَيْأً مِنَ الْأَشْعَارِ فَقَالَتْ أَسْمِعْنِي فَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla naʿam aʿrifu shayʾan mina al-ashʿāri fa-qālat asmiʿnī fa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And he said: Yes, I know something of the poems; and she said: Make-me-hear; and he recited, saying:
sentences.i: "Yes," he said, "I know a little poetry." "Let me hear it," she said. So he recited:

sentences.t:
هَنِيًّا مَرِيئًا غَيْرَ دَاءٍ مُخَامِرِ * لِعَزَّةَ مِنْ اَعْرَاضِنَا مَا اسْتَحَلَّتِ
فَوَاللَّهِ مَا قَارَبْتُ اِلَّانَبَا عَدَتْ بِصَرْمٍ * وَلَا اَكْثَرْتُ اِلَّا اَقَلَّتِ
اِنِّي وَتَهْيَامِي بِعَزَّةَ بَعْدَ مَا * تَخَلَّيْتُ مِمَّا بَيْنَنَا وَتَخَلَّتِ
لَكَالْمُرْتَجِي ظِلَّ الْغَمَامَةِ كُلَّمَا * تَبَوَّأ مِنْهَا لِلْمَقِيلِ اضْمَحَلَّتِ
sentences.tr:
hanīʾan marīʾan ghayra dāʾin mukhāmiri * li-ʿAzzata min aʿrāḍinā mā istaḥallati
fa-wa-Allāhi mā qārabtu illā nabā ʿadat bi-ṣarmin * wa-lā akthartu illā aqallati
innī wa-tahyāmī bi-ʿAzzata baʿda mā * takhallaytu mimmā baynanā wa-takhallati
la-ka-al-murtajī ẓilla al-ghamāmati kullamā * tabawwaʾa minhā li-al-maqīli iḍmaḥallati
sentences.l:
Wholesome, pleasant, without a lurking ailment, * to ʿAzza from our honours is what she has deemed lawful.
By God, I did not draw near but she shied, she sped off in a severing, * and I did not do much but she did less.
Indeed I, and my passion for ʿAzza, after * I withdrew from what is between us and she withdrew,
are like the one hoping for the shade of the cloud: whenever * he takes up a place from it for the midday rest, it dissolves.
sentences.i: May it do her good, a pleasure free of any lurking ailment: whatever of our honour she has made lawful is hers. By God, I never drew near but she shied away and broke with me, and I never gave much but she gave back less. Now that I have withdrawn from what lay between us, and she too has withdrawn, I and my passion for ʿAzza are like a man who hopes for the shade of a cloud: whenever he settles in it for the noon rest, it vanishes.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the edition prints it, vowel marks and all. The opening is a famous line of Kuthayyir to ʿAzza, in which he wishes her joy of whatever she has taken of his honour. اِلَّانَبَا is printed fused, and the line has a double space where the hemistichs divide; "but she shied (نَبَا), she sped off (عَدَتْ)" is a tentative reading, since the words may be a corruption of تَبَاعَدَتْ, "she drew away". The bare alif with kasra or fatḥa in اِنِّي, اِلَّا and اَقَلَّتِ is as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ مِنْهُ ذَلِكَ قَالَتْ لَقَدْ كَانَ كَثِيرٌ بَيِّنَ الْفَصَاحَةِ عَفِيفٌ وَبَالَغَ فِي وَصْفِهِ لِعَزَّةَ حَيْثُ قَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat minhu dhālika qālat la-qad kāna Kuthayyirun bayyina al-faṣāḥati ʿafīfun wa-bāligha fī waṣfihi li-ʿAzzata ḥaythu qāla
sentences.l: And when she heard that from him, she said: Truly Kuthayyir was clear-of the eloquence, chaste; and he went to extremes in his describing of ʿAzza where he said:
sentences.i: When she heard that from him, she said, "Kuthayyir was truly of manifest eloquence, and chaste, and he went far in his praise of ʿAzza when he said:"
sentences.n: بَيِّنَ الْفَصَاحَةِ (printed بيّن, with a shadda) is "plain in eloquence", an annexation; عَفِيفٌ follows without a connecting particle, as printed. Kuthayyir (Kuthayyir ʿAzza) is the poet of ʿAzza.

sentences.t: وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-anshadat taqūlu
sentences.l: And she recited, saying:
sentences.i: She went on to recite:

sentences.t:
لَوْاَنَّ عَزَّةَ حَاكَمَتْ شَمْسَ الضُّحَى * فِي الْحُسْنِ عِنْدَ مُوَفَّقٍ لَقَضَى لَهَا
وَسَعَى اِلَيَّ بِعَيْبِ عَزَّةَ نِسْوَةٌ * جَعَلَ الْاِلَهُ خُدُودَهُنَّ نِعَالَهَا
sentences.tr:
law anna ʿAzzata ḥākamat shamsa al-ḍuḥā * fī al-ḥusni ʿinda muwaffaqin la-qaḍā lahā
wa-saʿā ilayya bi-ʿaybi ʿAzzata niswatun * jaʿala al-ilāhu khudūdahunna niʿālahā
sentences.l:
If ʿAzza took the sun of the forenoon to judgement * in beauty, before one granted-success, he would have judged for her.
And women went-about to me with the fault of ʿAzza: * the God made their cheeks her sandals.
sentences.i: If ʿAzza were to bring the morning sun to judgement over beauty, before a judge guided aright he would rule for her. And certain women came running to me with talk of ʿAzza's faults; may God make their cheeks her sandals.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the edition prints it, vowel marks and all, including the fused لَوْاَنَّ and the bare alif with kasra in اِلَيَّ and الْاِلَهُ. The second line is both description and curse: جَعَلَ is the past tense used for a wish, "may He make".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُلْتُ وَقِيلَ إِنَّ عَزَّةَ كَانَتْ فِي نِهَايَةِ الْحُسْنِ وَالْجَمَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma qultu wa-qīla inna ʿAzzata kānat fī nihāyati al-ḥusni wa-al-jamāli
sentences.l: Then I said, and it was said, that ʿAzza was at the end of the beauty and the loveliness.
sentences.i: Then I said -- and it was said -- that ʿAzza was the very height of beauty and loveliness.
sentences.n: قُلْتُ ("I said") is printed so, where the sense wants قَالَتْ or قِيلَ (the narrator breaking in); it is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ يَا ابْنَ الْمَلِكِ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْرِفُ شَيْئًا مِنْ كَلَامِ جَمِيلٍ بُثَيْنَةَ فَأَنْشِدْنَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu yā ibna al-maliki in kunta taʿrifu shayʾan min kalāmi Jamīlin Buthaynata fa-anshidnā minhu
sentences.l: Then she said to him: O son of the king, if you know something of the speech of Jamīl, Buthayna, then make-us-recite from it.
sentences.i: Then she said to him, "Son of the king, if you know anything of the words of Jamīl, the poet of Buthayna, then recite some of them for us."
sentences.n: جَمِيلٍ بُثَيْنَةَ is the poet Jamīl, famed for his love of Buthayna; the second name is in apposition ("Jamīl of Buthayna").

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نَعَمْ أَنَا أَعْرَفُ بِهِ مِنْ كُلِّ أَحَدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla naʿam anā aʿrafu bihi min kulli aḥadin
sentences.l: And he said: Yes, I am more knowing with it than every one.
sentences.i: "Yes," he said, "I know him better than anyone."
sentences.n: أَعْرَفُ بِهِ is "better acquainted with him (or with his work)".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَ بِقَوْلٍ مِنْ شِعْرِ جَمِيلٍ هَذِهِ الْأَبْ اتَ
sentences.tr: thumma anshada bi-qawlin min shiʿri Jamīlin hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then he recited with a saying from the poetry of Jamīl these verses.
sentences.i: Then he recited these verses from the poetry of Jamīl.
sentences.n: بِقَوْلٍ is printed so; it is probably a slip for يَقُولُ ("saying"), but it is pointed as printed. The print breaks الأب—ات across the line and the archive keeps the halves apart (الْأَبْ اتَ), with the dash standing for the missing yāʾ; read al-abyāt, "the verses".

sentences.t:
يَقُولُونَ جَاهِدْ يَا جَمِيلُ بِغَزْوَةٍ * وَاَيُّ جِهَادٍ غَيْرُ هُنَّ اُرِيدُ
لِكُلِّ حَدِيثٍ بَيْنَهُنَّ بَشَاشَةٌ * وَكُلُّ فَتِيلٍ بَيْنَهُنَّ شَهِيدُ
اِذَا قُلْتُ مَابِي يَا بُثَيْنَةُ قَاتِلِي * مِنَ الْحُبِّ قَالَتْ ثَابِتٌ وَيَزِيدُ
وَاِنْ قُلْتُ رُدِّي بَعْضَ عَقْلِي اَعِشْ بِهِ * مَعَ النَّاسِ قَالَتْ ذَاكَ مِنْكَ بَعِيدُ
تُرِيدِينَ قَتْلِي لَاتُرِيدِينَ غَيْرَهُ * وَلَسْتُ اَرَى قَصْدًا سِوَاكَ اُرِيدُ
sentences.tr:
yaqūlūna jāhid yā Jamīlu bi-ghazwatin * wa-ayyu jihādin ghayru hunna urīdu
li-kulli ḥadīthin baynahunna bashāshatun * wa-kullu fatīlin baynahunna shahīdu
idhā qultu mā bī yā Buthaynatu qātilī * mina al-ḥubbi qālat thābitun wa-yazīdu
wa-in qultu ruddī baʿḍa ʿaqlī aʿish bihi * maʿa al-nāsi qālat dhāka minka baʿīdu
turīdīna qatlī lā turīdīna ghayrahu * wa-lastu arā qaṣdan siwāka urīdu
sentences.l:
They say: Strive, O Jamīl, in a raid; * and what striving other than them do I want?
For every talk among them is a gladness, * and every slain one among them is a martyr.
When I say, "What is in me, O Buthayna, is my killer, from love," * she says, "It is firm, and grows."
And if I say, "Give back some of my mind, that I may live by it among people," * she says, "That is far from you."
You want my killing, you do not want other than it, * and I see no aim but you that I want.
sentences.i: They tell me, "Jamīl, strive in a raid!" But what striving do I want other than these women? Every talk among them is a delight, and every man slain among them is a martyr. When I say, "Buthayna, what I feel is killing me with love," she answers, "It abides, and it grows." And if I say, "Give me back a little of my wits, that I may live among men," she answers, "That is far from you." You want my death and nothing more, and I see no goal but you that I want.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the edition prints it, with its own marks (the bare alifs in وَاَيُّ, اُرِيدُ, اِذَا, اَعِشْ, اَرَى are the print's). It is a famous complaint ascribed to Jamīl, lover of Buthayna: the "raid" is holy war, and the poet says his only campaign is among the women. The last line is the half-line that the girl's question in the next sentence quotes.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ ذَلِكَ قَالَتْ لَهُ أَحْسَنْتَ يَا ابْنَ الْمَلِكِ وَأَحْسَنَ جَمِيلٌ مَا الَّذِي أَرَادَتْهُ بُثَيْنَةُ بِجَمِيلٍ حَتَّى قَالَ هَذَا الشَّطْرَ أَيْ تُرِيدِينَ قَتْلِي لَاتُرِيدِينَ غَيْرَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat dhālika qālat lahu aḥsanta yā ibna al-maliki wa-aḥsana Jamīlun mā alladhī aradat-hu Buthaynatu bi-Jamīlin ḥattā qāla hādhā al-shaṭra ay turīdīna qatlī lā turīdīna ghayrahu
sentences.l: And when she heard that, she said to him: You have done well, O son of the king, and Jamīl did well. What is the-which Buthayna wanted of Jamīl, until he said this half-verse: "You want my killing, you do not want other than it"?
sentences.i: When she heard this, she said to him: Well done, son of the king, and well done Jamīl! But what did Buthayna want of Jamīl, that he spoke this hemistich, "You want my death, and want nothing else"?
sentences.n: أَيْ before the quotation means "namely"; the girl is asking what the line actually says Buthayna wants. شَطْر is a half-line (hemistich) of verse. لَاتُرِيدِينَ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا شَرْكَانُ يَا سَيِّدَتِي لَقَدْ أَرَادَتْ بِهِ مَا تُرِيدِينَ مِنِّي وَلَايُرْضِيكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā Sharkānu yā sayyidatī laqad aradat bihi mā turīdīna minnī wa-lā yurḍīki
sentences.l: And Sharkān said to her: O my lady, she indeed wanted by it what you want from me, and it does not please you.
sentences.i: Sharkān said to her: My lady, she meant by it just what you want of me, and it does not satisfy you either.
sentences.n: وَلَايُرْضِيكِ is printed as one word, and its sense is obscure: it may be a teasing remark that she too is not content until she has what she wants of him. We point it as the verb "it does not please you"; the print does not settle it.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَتْ لَمَّا قَالَ لَهَا شَرْكَانُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ وَلَمْ يَزَالَا يَشْرَبَانِ إِلَى أَنْ وَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالِاعْتِكَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥikat lammā qāla lahā Sharkānu hādhā al-kalāma wa-lam yazālā yashrabāni ilā an wallā al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri
sentences.l: And she laughed when Sharkān said to her this speech; and the two did not cease drinking until the day turned away and the night came on with the gloom.
sentences.i: She laughed when Sharkān spoke these words to her, and the two went on drinking until the day departed and night came on with its darkness.
sentences.n: لَمْ يَزَالَا is the dual: the prince and the girl. الِاعْتِكَار is the thickening of the night's darkness, as when dust or clouds gather.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَذَهَبَتْ إِلَى مَرْقَدِهَا وَنَامَتْ وَنَامَ شَرْكَانُ فِي مَقَامِهِ إِلَى أَنْ أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmati al-jāriyatu wa-dhahabat ilā marqadihā wa-nāmat wa-nāma Sharkānu fī maqāmihi ilā an aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu
sentences.l: And the girl rose and went to her place-of-lying and slept, and Sharkān slept in his place, until the morning became morning.
sentences.i: The girl rose and went to her bedchamber and slept, and Sharkān slept where he was, until morning came.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْجَوَارِي بِالدُّفُوفِ وَآلَاتِ الطَّرَبِ عَلَى الْعَادَةِ وَقَبَّلْنَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَقُلْنَ لَهُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ تَفَضَّلْ إِنَّ سَيِّدَتَنَا تَدْعُوكَ إِلَى الْحُضُورِ عِنْدَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqa aqbalat ʿalayhi al-jawārī bi-al-dufūfi wa-ālāti al-ṭarabi ʿalā al-ʿādati wa-qabbalna al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-qulna lahu bi-smi Allāhi tafaḍḍal inna sayyidatanā tadʿūka ilā al-ḥuḍūri ʿindahā
sentences.l: And when he awoke, the girls came to him with the tambourines and the instruments of mirth, according to the custom, and kissed the ground between his hands, and said to him: In the name of God, be gracious; indeed our lady calls you to the presence, with her.
sentences.i: When he woke, the girls came to him as before, with tambourines and instruments of music, and kissed the ground before him. They said to him: In God's name, be so kind; our mistress invites you to come into her presence.
sentences.n: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ here is the courteous word of invitation, "in God's name, please." بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, literally "between his two hands", means "in front of him".

sentences.t: فَقَامَ شَرْكَانُ وَمَشَى وَالْجَوَارِي حَوْلَهُ يَضْرِبْنَ بِالدُّفُوفِ وَآلَاتٍ إِلَى أَنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ تِلْكَ الدَّارِ وَدَخَلَ إِلَى دَارٍ غَيْرِهَا وَهِيَ أَعْظَمُ مِنَ الدَّارِ الْأُولَى وَفِيهَا مِنَ التَّمَاثِيلِ وَصُوَرِ الطُّيُورِ وَالْوُحُوشِ مَالَا يُوصَفُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma Sharkānu wa-mashā wa-al-jawārī ḥawlahu yaḍribna bi-al-dufūfi wa-ālātin ilā an kharaja min tilka al-dāri wa-dakhala ilā dārin ghayrihā wa-hiya aʿẓamu mina al-dāri al-ūlā wa-fīhā mina al-tamāthīli wa-ṣuwari al-ṭuyūri wa-al-wuḥūshi mālā yūṣafu
sentences.l: And Sharkān rose and walked, and the girls around him striking with the tambourines and instruments, until he went out from that house and entered a house other than it, and it was greater than the first house, and in it, of statues and forms of the birds and the wild beasts, what is not described.
sentences.i: Sharkān rose and walked on, the girls around him beating their tambourines and instruments, until he left that house and entered another, greater than the first. In it were statues and images of birds and wild beasts beyond description.
sentences.n: وَآلَاتٍ is left without its noun, as printed ("and instruments"). مَالَا يُوصَفُ is printed as one word. دَار means a whole house or palace complex, here a series of halls.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ شَرْكَانُ مِمَّا رَأَى مِنْ صَنْعَةِ ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ فَأَنْشَدَ يَقُ ولُ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba Sharkānu mimmā raʾā min ṣanʿati dhālika al-makāni fa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And Sharkān wondered at what he saw of the craft of that place, and he recited, saying:
sentences.i: Sharkān marvelled at the workmanship of the place and recited:
sentences.n: The print has يق—ول across a line break and the archive keeps the two halves apart, so we do too (يَقُ ولُ, read yaqūlu, "saying").

sentences.t:
اَجْنَى رَقِيبِي مِنْ ثِمَارِ قَلَائِدٍ * دُرَّ النُّحُورِ مُنَضَّدًا بِالْعَسْجَدِ
وَعُيُونِ مَاءٍ مِنْ سَبَائِكِ فِضَّةٍ * وَخُدُودِ وَرْدٍ فِي وُجُوهِ زَبَرْجَدِ
فَكَاَنَّمَا لَوْنُ الْبَنَفْسَجِ قَدْ حَكَى * زُرْقَ الْعُيُونِ وَكُحِّلَتْ بِالْاِثْمِدِ
sentences.tr:
ajnā raqībī min thimāri qalāʾidin * durra al-nuḥūri munaḍḍadan bi-al-ʿasjadi
wa-ʿuyūni māʾin min sabāʾiki fiḍḍatin * wa-khudūdi wardin fī wujūhi zabarjadi
fa-ka-annamā lawnu al-banafsaji qad ḥakā * zurqa al-ʿuyūni wa-kuḥḥilat bi-al-ithmidi
sentences.l:
My watcher gathered, of the fruits of necklaces, * the pearl of the throats, strung with gold,
and springs of water from ingots of silver, * and cheeks of rose in faces of emerald.
And as if the colour of the violet had imitated * the blue of eyes, kohl-lined with antimony.
sentences.i: My watcher gathered from the fruit of necklaces the pearls of throats, strung with gold; there were springs of water like ingots of silver, and rose-cheeks set in faces of emerald; and the violet's colour seemed to copy blue eyes lined with kohl.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the edition prints it, with its own marks. The scene is the palace garden pictured as a woman's adornment: flowers and fruit are jewels, water is silver, rose-petals are cheeks. رَقِيبِي, "my watcher", may be the gardener or the poet's guard; the poem leaves it open. In the last line the print has الْاِثْمِدِ with a bare alif carrying the kasra.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ شَرْكَانَ قَامَتْ لَهُ وَأَخَذَتْ بِيَدِهِ وَأَجْلَسَتْهُ إِلَى جَانِبِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾati al-jāriyatu Sharkāna qāmat lahu wa-akhadhat bi-yadihi wa-ajlasat-hu ilā jānibihā
sentences.l: And when the girl saw Sharkān, she rose for him, and took by his hand, and seated him beside her.
sentences.i: When the girl saw Sharkān, she rose to greet him, took him by the hand, and seated him at her side.
sentences.n: أَخَذَ بِيَدِهِ is "take him by the hand"; the verb takes the hand with بِـ.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَتُحْسِنُ شَيْئًا يَا ابْنَ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ فِي لَعِبِ الشِّطْرَنْجِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu a-tuḥsinu shayʾan yā ibna al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni fī laʿibi al-shiṭranji
sentences.l: And she said to him: Do you do well something, O son of the king ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, in the playing of chess?
sentences.i: Then she said to him: Son of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, are you at all skilled at chess?
sentences.n: أَتُحْسِنُ شَيْئًا, "do you do something well", is the idiom for "are you any good at it?". لَعِب is the verbal noun "playing"; الشِّطْرَنْج is chess, from Persian, and appears again in the poem below.

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ وَلَكِنْ لَا تَكُونِي كَمَا قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam wa-lākin lā takūnī ka-mā qāla al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: He said: Yes, but do not be as the poet said:
sentences.i: He said: I am, but do not be like the girl in the poet's lines.
sentences.n: The poem that follows is the player's complaint about an opponent whose game is all glances. The verb "be" is addressed to a woman (تَكُونِي).

sentences.t:
اَقُولُ وَالْوَجْدُ يَطْوِينِي وَيَنْشُرُنِي * وَنَهْلَةٌ مِنْ رُضَابِ الْحُبِّ تُرْوِينِي
حَضَرْتُ شِطْرَنْجَ مَنْ اَهْوَى فَلَاعَبَنِي * بِالْبِيضِ وَالسُّودِ لَكِنْ لَيْسَ يُرْضِينِي
كَاَنَّمَا الشَّاهُ عِنْدَ الرُّخِّ مَوْضِعُهُ * وَقَدْ تَفَقَّدَ دَسْتًا بِالْفَرَازِينِ
فَانْ نَظَرْتُ اِلَى مَعْنَى لَوَاحِظِهَا * فَغُنْجُ اَلْحَاظِهَا يَا قَوْمِ يُرْدِينِي
sentences.tr:
aqūlu wa-al-wajdu yaṭwīnī wa-yanshurunī * wa-nahlatun min ruḍābi al-ḥubbi turwīnī
ḥaḍartu shiṭranja man ahwā fa-lāʿabanī * bi-al-bīḍi wa-al-sūdi lākin laysa yurḍīnī
ka-annamā al-shāhu ʿinda al-rukhkhi mawḍiʿuhu * wa-qad tafaqqada dastan bi-al-farāzīni
fa-in naẓartu ilā maʿnā lawāḥiẓihā * fa-ghunju alḥāẓihā yā qawmi yurdīnī
sentences.l:
I say, while passion folds me and unfolds me, * and a sip of the spittle of love waters me:
I attended the chess of one I love, and she played me * with the whites and the blacks, but it does not please me.
As if the king's place were beside the rook, * and he had sought out a hand among the queens.
And if I look to the meaning of her glances, * then the coquetry of her eyes, O people, destroys me.
sentences.i: I say, while longing folds me up and spreads me out, and one sip of love's sweet spittle would quench me: I sat down to the chess of my beloved and she played me, white against black, but it gave me no content. It is as though the king's place were beside the rook, and he were searching for a move among the queens. And if I look to the sense of her glances, the coquetry of her eyes, my people, destroys me.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the edition prints it, with its own marks (the bare alifs in اَقُولُ, اَهْوَى, كَاَنَّمَا, اَلْحَاظِهَا and the rest are the print's). The chess terms are الشَّاه (king), الرُّخّ (rook), الْفَرَازِين (queens, sing. فِرْزَان) and دَسْت, a Persian word for a hand or move in a game. The poet is distracted from the board by the lady's eyes.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَدَّمَتْ لَهُ الشِّطْرَنْجَ وَلَعِبَتْ مَعَهُ فَصَارَ شَرْكَانُ كُلَّمَا أَرَادَأَنْ يَنْظُرَ إِلَى نَقْلِهَا نَظَرَ إِلَى وَجْهِهَا فَيَضَعُ الْفَرَسَ مَوْضِعَ الْفِيلِ وَيَضَعُ الْفِيلَ مَوْضِعَ الْفَرَسِ
sentences.tr: thumma qaddamat lahu al-shiṭranja wa-laʿibat maʿahu fa-ṣāra Sharkānu kullamā arāda an yanẓura ilā naqlihā naẓara ilā wajhihā fa-yaḍaʿu al-farasa mawḍiʿa al-fīli wa-yaḍaʿu al-fīla mawḍiʿa al-farasi
sentences.l: Then she presented to him the chess, and played with him; and Sharkān became, whenever he wanted that he look to her moving-of-the-pieces, he looked to her face, and put the horse in the place of the elephant and put the elephant in the place of the horse.
sentences.i: Then she set the chess before him and played with him. But whenever Sharkān meant to follow her moves, he looked at her face instead, and so he put the knight where the bishop belonged and the bishop where the knight belonged.
sentences.n: الْفَرَس (horse) and الْفِيل (elephant) are the knight and the bishop of the chess board, which is why the mix-up is comic. أَرَادَأَنْ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَتْ وَقَٰلَتْ إِنْ كَانَ لَعِبُكَ هَكَذَا فَإِنَّكَ لَاتَعْرِفُ شَيْئًا
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥikat wa-qālat in kāna laʿibuka hākadhā fa-innaka lā taʿrifu shayʾan
sentences.l: And she laughed and said: If your playing was thus, then indeed you, you do not know a thing.
sentences.i: She laughed and said, "If this is how you play, you know nothing at all."
sentences.n: The print has قلت, which taken at face value would be "I said"; since the girl is the subject, we read it as a defective spelling of قَالَتْ "she said" and mark it with the dagger alif. لَاتَعْرِفُ is printed as one word; شَيْئًا keeps the print's ئ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ هَذَا أَوَّلُ دَسْتٍ لَاتَحْسِبِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla hādhā awwalu dastin lā taḥsibīhi
sentences.l: And he said: This is the first of a round; do not count it (f.).
sentences.i: He said, "This is only the first round; do not count it against me."
sentences.n: دَسْت (Persian dast, "hand") is a round or game at chess and similar pastimes. لَاتَحْسِبِيهِ is printed as one word: lā plus the feminine jussive, "do not (you, f.) reckon it".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا غَلَبَتْهُ رَجَعَ وَصَفَّ الْقِطَعَ وَلَعِبَ مَعَهَا فَغَلَبَتْهُ ثَانِيًا وَثَالِثًا وَرَابِعًا وَخَامِسًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ghalabat-hu rajaʿa wa-ṣaffa al-qiṭaʿa wa-laʿiba maʿahā fa-ghalabat-hu thāniyan wa-thālithan wa-rābiʿan wa-khāmisan
sentences.l: And when she overcame him, he returned and lined up the pieces and played with her; and she overcame him secondly and thirdly and fourthly and fifthly.
sentences.i: When she had beaten him, he went back, set out the pieces again and played on; but she beat him a second time, a third, a fourth and a fifth.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَنْتَ فِي كُلِّ شَيْئٍ مَغْلُوبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafatat ilayhi wa-qālat lahu anta fī kulli shayʾin maghlūbun
sentences.l: And she turned to him and said to him: You, in every thing, [are] overcome.
sentences.i: Then she turned to him and said, "You are beaten at everything."
sentences.n: شَيْئٍ is printed with a final ئ (the print's spelling); read it as شَيْءٍ, "a thing". مَغْلُوبٌ is the predicate: "you are beaten".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَاسَيِّدَتِي عَلَى مَنْ لَاعَبَ مِثْلَكِ كَيْفَ لَايُغْلَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidatī ʿalā man lāʿaba mithlaki kayfa lā yughlabu
sentences.l: And he said: O my lady, upon whom plays the like-of-you, how is he not overcome?
sentences.i: He said, "My lady, when a man plays against one such as you, how could he not be beaten?"
sentences.n: لايُغْلَبُ carries a damma on the yāʾ in the print, which we keep. عَلَى مَنْ لَاعَبَ مِثْلَكِ is clipped: "against whoever plays your like". يَاسَيِّدَتِي and لَايُغْلَبُ are each printed as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَتْ بِإِحْضَارِ الطَّعَامِ فَأَكَلَا وَغَسَلَا أَيْدِيَهُمَا وَقَدَّمُوا لَهُمَا الشَّرَابَ فَشَرِبَا
sentences.tr: thumma amarat bi-iḥḍāri al-ṭaʿāmi fa-akalā wa-ghasalā aydiyahumā wa-qaddamū lahumā al-sharāba fa-sharibā
sentences.l: Then she commanded the bringing-present of the food, and the two ate and the two washed their hands, and they presented to the two the drink, and the two drank.
sentences.i: Then she ordered food to be brought, and the two ate and washed their hands; drink was set before them, and the two drank.
sentences.n: وَقَدَّمُوا has no stated subject; it means the servants, so "drink was set before them".

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَخَذَتِ الْقَانُونَ وَكَانَ لَهَا يَدٌفِي ضَرْبِ الْقَانُونِ فَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika akhadhati al-qānūna wa-kāna lahā yadun fī ḍarbi al-qānūni fa-anshadat taqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And after that she took the zither, and there was to her a hand in the striking of the zither; and she recited, saying these verses.
sentences.i: After that she took up the zither, for she had a skilled hand at playing it, and she recited these verses.
sentences.n: الْقَانُون is the qānūn, a plucked trapezoid zither. يَدٌفِي is printed as one word, "a hand in"; having a hand in something means being skilled at it.

sentences.t:
اَلدَّهْرُ مَابَيْنَ مَطْوِيٍّ وَمَبْسُوطِ * وَمِثْلُهُ مِثْلُ مَجْرُورٍ وَمَخْرُوطِ
فَاشْرَبْ عَلَى حُسْنِهِ اِنْكُنْتَ مُقْتَدِرًا * اَنْ لَاتُفَارِقَنِي فِي وَجْهِ تَفْرِيطِ
sentences.tr:
al-dahru mā bayna maṭwiyyin wa-mabsūṭi * wa-mithluhu mithlu majrūrin wa-makhrūṭi
fa-ishrab ʿalā ḥusnihi in kunta muqtadiran * an lā tufāriqanī fī wajhi tafrīṭi
sentences.l:
Time: it is between folded and spread-out * and its like is the like of dragged and lathe-turned.
So drink upon its beauty, if you are able, * that you not part from me in any face of neglect.
sentences.i: Time is now folded up, now spread out, and its like is something dragged and something turned on the lathe; so drink to its beauty, if you can, and never part from me through any neglect.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the edition prints it, marks and all. مَابَيْنَ and اِنْكُنْتَ are printed fused. The first line is hard: "folded" and "spread out" suggest a scroll or a carpet, and مَجْرُور ("dragged") with مَخْرُوط ("turned on a lathe") may be a play on grammar and craft words, but the sense is uncertain and the translation is a reading.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّمَا لَمْ يَزَالَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَ اللَّيْلُ فَكَانَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ أَحْسَنَ مِنَ الْيَوْمِ الْأَوَّلِ
sentences.tr: thumma innamā lam yazālā ʿalā dhālika ilā an dakhala al-laylu fa-kāna fī dhālika al-yawmi aḥsana mina al-yawmi al-awwali
sentences.l: Then only, the two did not cease upon that until the night entered; and it was, in that day, better than the first day.
sentences.i: And so the two went on until night came, and that day was lovelier than the first.
sentences.n: أَحْسَنَ is accusative as printed (the predicate of a كَانَ with no stated subject, "it was better"). Read the sentence as "it was better" with the day itself as the point of comparison.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ مَضَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ إِلَى مَرْقَدِهَا وَلَمْ يَبْقَ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا الْجَوَارِي فَأَلْقَى نَفْسَهُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَنَامَ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbala al-laylu maḍati al-jāriyatu ilā marqadihā wa-lam yabqa ʿindahu illā al-jawārī fa-alqā nafsahu ʿalā al-arḍi wa-nāma ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And when the night approached, the girl went to her place-of-lying, and there did not remain with him except the girls; and he threw himself upon the ground and slept to the morning.
sentences.i: When night drew on, the girl went off to her bedchamber, and no one was left with him but the girls; so he cast himself down on the floor and slept until morning.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْجَوَارِي عَلَى عَادَتِهَا بِالدُّفُوفِ وَآلَاتِ الطَّرَبِ فَلَمَّا رَآهَا نَهَضَ وَجَلَسَ وَأَخَذْنَهُ وَمَشَيْنَ بِهِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى الْجَارِيَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbalat ʿalayhi al-jawārī ʿalā ʿādatihā bi-al-dufūfi wa-ālāti al-ṭarabi fa-lammā raʾāhā nahaḍa wa-jalasa wa-akhadhnahu wa-mashayna bihi ilā an waṣalū ilā al-jāriyati
sentences.l: And the girls came toward him, according to her custom, with the tambourines and the instruments of mirth; and when he saw her, he rose and sat, and they (f.) took him and they (f.) walked with him until they (m.) arrived at the girl.
sentences.i: Then the girls came to him as they always did, with tambourines and instruments of merriment. When he saw them he rose and sat up, and they took him and walked with him until they came to the girl.
sentences.n: Agreement wanders here, as often in Middle Arabic: الْجَوَارِي ("the girls") is treated as a feminine singular in عَادَتِهَا and رَآهَا, as feminine plural in أَخَذْنَهُ and مَشَيْنَ, and as masculine plural in وَصَلُوا.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ نَهَضَتْ قَائِمَةً وَأَخَذَتْ بِيَدِهِ وَأَجْلَسَتْهُ إِلَى جَانِبِهَا وَسَأَلَتْهُ عَنْ مَبِيتِهِ فَدَعَا لَهَا بِطُولِ الْبَقَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾat-hu nahaḍat qāʾimatan wa-akhadhat bi-yadihi wa-ajlasat-hu ilā jānibihā wa-saʾalat-hu ʿan mabītihi fa-daʿā lahā bi-ṭūli al-baqāʾi
sentences.l: And when she saw him, she rose, standing, and took by his hand, and had-him-sit to her side, and asked him about his night-lodging; and he prayed for her with length of remaining.
sentences.i: When she saw him, she rose to her feet, took him by the hand, seated him beside her and asked how he had passed the night; and he prayed that she might live long.
sentences.n: مَبِيت is the spending of the night. دَعَا لَهَا بِطُولِ الْبَقَاءِ is the stock courtesy of wishing someone a long life.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتِ الْعُودَ وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhati al-ʿūda wa-anshadat taqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: And she took the lute and recited, saying: poetry.
sentences.i: Then she took up the lute and sang this poem.
sentences.n: The single word شعر, "poetry", stands in the print where the usual phrase would be "these verses".

sentences.t:
لَا تَرْكُنَنَّ اِلَى الْفِرَاقِ فَاِنَّهُ * مُرُّ الْمَذَاقِ
اَلشَّمْسُ عِنْدَ غُرُوبِهَا * تَصْفَرُّ مِنْ اَلَمِ الْفِرَاقِ
sentences.tr:
lā tarkunanna ilā al-firāqi fa-innahu * murru al-madhāqi
al-shamsu ʿinda ghurūbihā * taṣfarru min alami al-firāqi
sentences.l:
Do not incline to separation, for it * is bitter of taste.
The sun, at its setting, * turns yellow from the pain of separation.
sentences.i: Never lean on parting, for it is bitter to the taste. The sun at its setting turns pale with the pain of parting.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the edition prints it, bare-alif hamza marks and all. The first line is printed as one stretch with a double space where the halves meet, and the second half is short; we place the break there.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمَا عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ وَإِذَا هُمَا بِضَجَّةٍ وَرِجَالٍ مُتَزَاحِمِينَ وَبَطَارِقَةٍ بِأَيْدِيهِمُ السُّيُوفُ مَسْلُولَةً تَلْمَعُ وَهُمْ يَقُولُونَ بِلِسَانِ الرُّومِيَّةِ وَقَعْتَ عِنْدَنَا يَا شَرْكَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā humā ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati wa-idhā humā bi-ḍajjatin wa-rijālin mutazāḥimīna wa-baṭāriqatin bi-aydīhimi al-suyūfu maslūlatan talmaʿu wa-hum yaqūlūna bi-lisāni al-rūmiyyati waqaʿta ʿindanā yā Sharkānu
sentences.l: And while the two of them were upon this state, and behold the two of them with a clamour, and men crowding, and patricians, in their hands the swords drawn, gleaming, and they saying in the tongue of the Greek: You have fallen with us, O Sharkān.
sentences.i: While the two of them were in this state, behold, there was a clamour, and men thronging in, and patricians with drawn swords gleaming in their hands, and they were crying in the Greek tongue: You have fallen into our hands, Sharkān!
sentences.n: وَإِذَا هُمَا بِـ is the "behold" idiom: بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what appears. بِأَيْدِيهِمُ السُّيُوفُ مَسْلُولَةً is a circumstantial clause, "swords drawn in their hands". الرُّومِيَّة is the language of the Rūm, here the Byzantine Greek of the Christian court. وَقَعْتَ عِنْدَنَا is the soldiers' taunt: "you have fallen with us", that is, into our hands.

sentences.t: فَأَيْقَنَ بِالْهَلَاكِ
sentences.tr: fa-ayqana bi-al-halāki
sentences.l: And he became certain of the destruction.
sentences.i: He was certain he was lost.
sentences.n: أَيْقَنَ بِـ takes its object with بِـ: "be certain of".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ قَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Sharkānu hādhā al-kalāma qāla fī nafsihi
sentences.l: And when Sharkān heard this speech, he said in his self,
sentences.i: When Sharkān heard these words, he said to himself:

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَمِلَتْ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةُ الْحِيلَةَ وَأَمْهَلَتْنِي إِلَى أَنْ جَاءَتْ رِجَالُهَا وَهُمُ الْبَطَارِقَةُ الَّذِينَ خَوَّفَتْنِي بِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi la-qad ʿamilat hādhihi al-jāriyatu al-ḥīlata wa-amhalat-nī ilā an jāʾat rijāluhā wa-humu al-baṭāriqatu alladhīna khawwafat-nī bi-him
sentences.l: By God, this girl has indeed worked the trick, and she gave-me-respite until her men came, and they are the patricians whom she made-me-afraid with.
sentences.i: By God, this girl has played her trick! She gave me time until her men arrived, and they are the very patricians she threatened me with.
sentences.n: لَقَدْ عَمِلَتْ: لَـ with قَدْ gives emphasis, "has indeed worked". جَاءَتْ رِجَالُهَا has a feminine verb before a broken plural, which Classical grammar allows. خَوَّفَ بِـ is "to frighten with".

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ أَنَا الَّذِي قَدْ أَلْقَيْتُ نَفْسِي فِي هَذَا الْهَلَاكِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin anā alladhī qad alqaytu nafsī fī hādhā al-halāki
sentences.l: But I am the one who has cast my self into this destruction.
sentences.i: But it is I who have cast myself into this ruin.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى الْجَارِيَةِ لِيُعَاتِبَهَا فَوَجَدَ وَجْهَهَا قَدْ تَغَيَّرَ بِالِاصْفِرَارِ
sentences.tr: thumma iltafata ilā al-jāriyati li-yuʿātibahā fa-wajada wajhahā qad taghayyara bi-al-iṣfirāri
sentences.l: Then he turned to the girl to reproach her, and found her face had changed with yellowing.
sentences.i: Then he turned to the girl to reproach her, and found that her face had changed and gone pale.
sentences.n: بِالِاصْفِرَارِ is "with yellowing", the pallor of fear; the بِـ says by what means her face had changed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَثَبَتْ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهَا وَهِيَ تَقُولُ لَهُمْ مَنْ أَنْتُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma wathabat ʿalā qadamayhā wa-hiya taqūlu lahum man antum
sentences.l: Then she leapt upon her two feet, and she saying to them: Who are you?
sentences.i: Then she sprang to her feet and said to them: Who are you?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الْبَطْرِيقُ الْمُقَدَّمُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَيَّتُهَا الْمَلِكَةُ الْكَرِيمَةُ وَالدُّرَّةُ الْيَتِيمَةُ أَمَا تَعْرِفِينَ مَنْ هُوَ الَّذِي عِنْدَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-baṭrīqu al-muqaddamu ʿalayhim ayyatuhā al-malikatu al-karīmatu wa-al-durratu al-yatīmatu a-mā taʿrifīna man huwa alladhī ʿindaki
sentences.l: And the patrician, the one-put-forward over them, said to her: O queen, the noble, and pearl, the unmatched, do you not know who he is, the one with you?
sentences.i: Then the patrician who led them said to her: O noble queen, O peerless pearl, do you not know who it is that is with you?
sentences.n: الدُّرَّةُ الْيَتِيمَة, "the orphan pearl", is the jeweller's phrase for a pearl without its like. أَيَّتُهَا is printed ايتها and is pointed as the usual vocative form. الْمُقَدَّم عَلَيْهِمْ is "the one set at their head".

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ لَاأَعْرِفُهُ فَمَنْ يَكُونُ هَذَا
sentences.tr: qālat lahu lā aʿrifuhu fa-man yakūnu hādhā
sentences.l: She said to him: I do not know him; so who is this?
sentences.i: She said to him: I do not know him. Who can he be?
sentences.n: لَاأَعْرِفُهُ is printed as one word, لا and the verb run together.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا هَذَا مُخَرِّبُ الْبُلْدَانِ وَسَيِّدُ الْفُرْسَانِ هَذَا شَرْكَانُ بْنُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ هَذَا الَّذِي فَتَحَ الْقِلَاعَ وَمَلَكَ كُلَّ حِصْنٍ مَنَاعٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā hādhā mukharribu al-buldāni wa-sayyidu al-fursāni hādhā Sharkānu bnu al-maliki ʿUmara bni al-Nuʿmāni hādhā alladhī fataḥa al-qilāʿa wa-malaka kulla ḥiṣnin manāʿin
sentences.l: And he said to her: This is the ruiner-of the lands and lord-of the horsemen; this is Sharkān, son of King ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān; this is the one who opened the fortresses and took-possession-of every fortress, a forbidding one.
sentences.i: He said to her: This is the destroyer of lands and the lord of horsemen. This is Sharkān, son of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, who has opened fortresses and seized every stronghold, however strong.
sentences.n: مَنَاعٍ is printed as it stands; the usual word for an impregnable fortress is مَنِيع, and مَنَّاع, "very forbidding, withholding", is the nearest reading of the letters.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ وَصَلَ خَبَرُهُ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ وَالِدِكِ مِنَ السَّيِّدَةِ الْعَجُوزِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: wa-qad waṣala khabaruhu ilā al-maliki Ḥardūba wālidiki mina al-sayyidati al-ʿajūzi dhāti al-dawāhī
sentences.l: And his news has reached King Ḥardūb, your father, from the lady, the old woman, owner-of the calamities.
sentences.i: His news has reached King Ḥardūb, your father, from the old woman, the Lady of Calamities.
sentences.n: الْمَلِكَ حَرْدُوبَ is Ḥardūb, the girl's father in this tale. ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي, "mistress of calamities", is the old woman's nickname; the name is a tag rather than a title.

sentences.t: وَتَحَقَّقَ ذَلِكَ وَالِدُكِ مَلِكُنَا نَقْلًا عَنِ الْعَجُوزِوَهَا أَنْتِ قَدْ نَصَرْتِ عَسْكَرَ الرُّومِ بِأَخْذِ هَذَا الْأَسَدِ الْمَشْئُومِ
sentences.tr: wa-taḥaqqaqa dhālika wāliduki malikunā naqlan ʿani al-ʿajūzi wa-hā anti qad naṣarti ʿaskara al-rūmi bi-akhdhi hādhā al-asadi al-mashʾūmi
sentences.l: And confirmed that your father, our king, by report from the old woman-and-lo: you have helped the army of the Greeks by the taking of this lion, the ill-omened.
sentences.i: Your father, our king, has confirmed it on the old woman's report. And now you have given the army of the Greeks the victory by capturing this ill-starred lion.
sentences.n: الْعَجُوزِوَهَا is two words printed run together: الْعَجُوزِ "the old woman" and وَهَا, "and lo", which opens the next clause. هَا أَنْتِ, "here you are", is split by the و in print. The verb تَحَقَّقَ has its subject after it: "your father, our king, confirmed that". نَصَرْتِ is addressed to the girl (feminine -ti).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَ الْبَطْرِيقِ نَظَرَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ مَا اسْمُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāma al-baṭrīqi naẓarat ilayhi wa-qālat lahu mā ismuka
sentences.l: And when she heard the speech of the patrician, she looked at him and said to him: What is your name?
sentences.i: When she had heard the patrician's words, she looked at him and asked: What is your name?

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهَا اسْمِي مَاسُورَةُ بْنُ عَهْدِكَ مُوسُورَةَ بْنِ كَاشْرَدَهْ بَطْرِيقُ الْبَطَارِنَةِ
sentences.tr: qāla lahā ismī Māsūratu bnu ʿahdika Mūsūrata bni Kāshradah baṭrīqu al-baṭārinati
sentences.l: He said to her: My name is Māsūra, son of your covenant, Mūsūra, son of Kāsharda, patrician of the patricians.
sentences.i: He said to her: My name is Māsūra, son of Mūsūra son of Kāsharda, chief of the patricians.
sentences.n: بْنُ عَهْدِكَ, "son of your covenant", is obscure and may be a corrupt or misplaced word, perhaps a scribe's "your servant" or an epithet; we point it as printed and give it in the literal line only. الْبَطَارِنَة is printed for الْبَطَارِقَة, "patricians", and is kept as printed. The names are Greek-sounding inventions of the storyteller.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ وَكَيْفَ دَخَلْتَ عَلَيَّ بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِي
sentences.tr: qālat lahu wa-kayfa dakhalta ʿalayya bi-ghayri idhnī
sentences.l: She said to him: And how did you enter upon me without my leave?
sentences.i: She said to him: And how did you come in to me without my leave?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا يَا مَوْلَاتِي إِنِّي لَمَّا وَصَلْتُ إِلَى الْبَابِ مَامَنَعَنِي حَاجِبٌ وَلَابَوَّابٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā yā mawlātī innī lammā waṣaltu ilā al-bābi mā manaʿanī ḥājibun wa-lā bawwābun
sentences.l: And he said to her: O my mistress, when I arrived at the gate, no chamberlain stopped me, and no doorkeeper.
sentences.i: He said to her: My lady, when I reached the gate, neither chamberlain nor doorkeeper stopped me,
sentences.n: مَامَنَعَنِي and وَلَابَوَّابٌ are each printed as one word, with the negative run into what follows.

sentences.t: بَلْ قَامَ جَمِيعُ الْبَوَّابِينَ وَمَشَوْابَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا كَمَا جَرَتْ بِهِ الْعَادَةُ إِنَّهُ إِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدٌ غَيْرُنَا يَتْرُكُونَهُ وَاقِفًا عَلَى الْبَابِ حَتَّى يَسْتَأْذِنُوا عَلَيْهِ بِالدُّخُولِ
sentences.tr: bal qāma jamīʿu al-bawwābīna wa-mashaw bayna aydīnā ka-mā jarat bihi al-ʿādatu innahu idhā jāʾa aḥadun ghayrunā yatrukūnahu wāqifan ʿalā al-bābi ḥattā yastaʾdhinū ʿalayhi bi-al-dukhūli
sentences.l: But all the doorkeepers rose and walked between our hands, as the custom has run with it, that when anyone other than us comes, they leave him standing at the door until they ask-leave for him for the entering.
sentences.i: No, all the doorkeepers rose and walked before us, as is the custom: if anyone but us comes, they leave him standing at the door until they have asked leave for him to enter.
sentences.n: وَمَشَوْابَيْنَ is printed as one word; read وَمَشَوْا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا, "and they walked before us" (literally "between our hands"). جَرَتْ بِهِ الْعَادَةُ, "the custom ran with it", means "as is the custom". يَسْتَأْذِنُوا عَلَيْهِ is "ask admission for him"; the edition prints the hamza here.

sentences.t: وَلَيْسَ هَذَا وَقْتَ إِطَالَةِ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-laysa hādhā waqta iṭālati al-kalāmi
sentences.l: And this is not the time of prolonging the speech.
sentences.i: And this is no time for long speeches.

sentences.t: وَالْمَلِكُ مُنْتَظِرٌ رُجُوعَنَا إِلَيْهِ بِهَذَا الْمَلِكِ الَّذِي هُوَ شَوْكَةُ عَسْكَرِ الْإِسْلَامِ حَتَّى إِنَّهُ يَقْتُلُهُ وَيَرْحَلُ عَسْكَرُهُ إِلَى الْمَوْضِعِ الَّذِي جَاوُا مِنْهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَحْصُلَ لَنَا تَعَبٌ فِي قِتَالِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-al-maliku muntaẓirun rujūʿanā ilayhi bi-hādhā al-maliki alladhī huwa shawkatu ʿaskari al-islāmi ḥattā innahu yaqtuluhu wa-yarḥalu ʿaskaruhu ilā al-mawḍiʿi alladhī jāʾū minhu min ghayri an yaḥṣula lanā taʿabun fī qitālihim
sentences.l: And the king is awaiting our return to him with this king, who is the thorn of the army of Islam, so that he kills him and his army departs to the place which they came from, without there befalling us toil in fighting them.
sentences.i: The king is waiting for us to come back to him with this king, the thorn in the side of the army of Islam, so that he may kill him and have his army march off to the place it came from, without our having to toil at fighting them.
sentences.n: جَاوُا is printed جاوا for جَاؤُوا, "they came"; the edition drops the hamza-carrying wāw, and we point the letters as printed. بِهَذَا الْمَلِكِ means "with this prince": the patrician calls Sharkān "king" loosely, as a king's son. حَتَّى إِنَّهُ يَقْتُلُهُ is "so that he kills him".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ مِنْهُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ قَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ غَيْرُ حَسَنٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-jāriyatu minhu hādhā al-kalāma qālat lahu inna hādhā al-kalāma ghayru ḥasanin
sentences.l: And when the girl heard from him this speech, she said to him: Indeed this speech is not good.
sentences.i: When the girl heard these words from him, she said to him, "What you have said is not well said."

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ قَدْ كَذَبَتِ السِّتُّ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي فَإِنَّهَا قَدْ تَكَلَّمَتْ بِكَلَامٍ بَاطِلٍ وَهِيَ لَا تَعْلَمُ حَقِيقَتَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin qad kadhabati al-sittu dhātu al-dawāhī fa-innahā qad takallamat bi-kalāmin bāṭilin wa-hiya lā taʿlamu ḥaqīqatahu
sentences.l: But the lady, owner-of the calamities, has lied, for she has spoken with a speech false, and she does not know its truth.
sentences.i: But the Lady of Calamities has lied; she has spoken falsehood, and she does not know the truth of it.
sentences.n: السِّتُّ is the Middle Arabic and colloquial "lady" (for سَيِّدَة); ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي "mistress of calamities" is the old queen's nickname.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ إِنَّ الَّذِي عِنْدِي مَا هُوَ شَرْكَانُ وَلَا هُوَ أَسِيرٌ وَلَكِنَّهُ رَجُلٌ أَتَى إِلَيْنَا وَقَدِمَ عَلَيْنَا وَطَلَبَ الضِّيَافَةَ فَأَضَفْنَاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-anā wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi inna alladhī ʿindī mā huwa Sharkānu wa-lā huwa asīrun wa-lākinnahu rajulun atā ilaynā wa-qadima ʿalaynā wa-ṭalaba al-ḍiyāfata fa-aḍafnāhu
sentences.l: And I, by the right of the Messiah: the one who is with me is not Sharkān, nor is he a captive, but he is a man who came to us and arrived upon us and asked for hospitality, so we hosted him.
sentences.i: As for me, by the Messiah, the man who is with me is not Sharkān, nor is he a prisoner. He is a man who came to us, arrived among us and asked for hospitality, and we have received him as our guest.
sentences.n: ما هُوَ شَرْكَانُ and وَلَا هُوَ أَسِيرٌ are verbless negations with مَا and لَا plus a pronoun, a colloquial pattern, and the nominative is kept as printed. وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ is an oath: "by the right of the Messiah".

sentences.t: فَإِنْ تَحَقَّقْنَا أَنَّهُ شَرْكَانُ بِعَيْنِهِ وَثَبَتَ عِنْدَنَا أَنَّهُ هُوَ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَكٍّ فَلَا يَلِيقُ بِمُرُوَّتِي إِنِّي أُمَكِّنُكُمْ عَلَى مَنْ دَخَلَ تَحْتَ ذِمَامِي
sentences.tr: fa-in taḥaqqaqnā annahu Sharkānu bi-ʿaynihi wa-thabata ʿindanā annahu huwa min ghayri shakkin fa-lā yalīqu bi-muruwwatī innī umakkinukum ʿalā man dakhala taḥta dhimāmī
sentences.l: So if we ascertain that he is Sharkān in his very self, and it is established with us that he is he, from without doubt, then it does not befit my manliness that I give-you-power over one who entered under my protection.
sentences.i: If we learn that he is Sharkān himself, and it is established beyond doubt that he is the man, even so it does not become my honour to give you power over one who has entered under my protection.
sentences.n: مُرُوَّتِي is pointed muruwwa, the spelling the print supports (without hamza); the classical word is مُرُوءَة, "manly honour". بِعَيْنِهِ is "in his very self". أُمَكِّنُكُمْ عَلَى is "give you power over" with عَلَى, a construction of the later language.

sentences.t: فَلَا تَخُونُونِي فِي ضَيْفِي وَلَا تَفْضَحُونِي بَيْنَ الْأَنَامِ بَلِ ارْجِعْ أَنْتَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ أَبِي وَقَبِّلِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَخْبِرْهُ بِأَنَّ الْأَمْرَ بِخِلَافِ مَا قَالَتِ السِّتُّ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-lā takhūnūnī fī ḍayfī wa-lā tafḍaḥūnī bayna al-anāmi bal irjiʿ anta ilā al-maliki abī wa-qabbili al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-akhbirhu bi-anna al-amra bi-khilāfi mā qālati al-sittu dhātu al-dawāhī
sentences.l: So do not betray me in my guest, and do not disgrace me among mankind; rather return, you, to the king my father, and kiss the earth between his two hands, and inform him that the matter is contrary to what the lady, owner-of the calamities, said.
sentences.i: So do not betray me over my guest, and do not shame me before the world. Rather, go back to the king my father, kiss the ground before him, and tell him that the matter is contrary to what the Lady of Calamities said.
sentences.n: قَبِّلِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, "kiss the earth between his hands", is the courtly formula for doing homage before a king.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْبِطْرِيقُ مَا سُورَةُ يَا أَبْرِيزَةُ أَنَا مَا أَقْدِرُ أَنْ أَعُودَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ إِلَّا بِغَرِيمِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-biṭrīqu mā sūratu yā Abrīzatu anā mā aqdiru an aʿūda ilā al-maliki illā bi-gharīmihi
sentences.l: And the patrician said: What a form, O Abrīza! I cannot return to the king except with his adversary.
sentences.i: The patrician said, "Never, Abrīza! I cannot go back to the king except with his enemy."
sentences.n: مَا سُورَةُ (printed so; perhaps for مَا صُورَةُ, "what shape") is an obscure exclamation of refusal that recurs in this scene; "No, never" is a reading from the context, not a certainty. غَرِيم is "adversary, debtor", here the enemy whom he is bound to take.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ وَقَدِ اغْتَاظَتْ وَيْلَكَ عُذِّلْهُ بِالْجَوَابِ وَلَا عَلَيْكَ مَلَامٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu wa-qadi ightāẓat waylaka ʿudhdhilhu bi-al-jawābi wa-lā ʿalayka malāmun
sentences.l: And she said to him, and she had become enraged: Woe to you! Reproach him with the answer, and no blame is upon you.
sentences.i: Enraged, she said to him, "Woe to you! Take him to task with your answer, and no blame will fall on you."
sentences.n: عُذِّلْهُ carries a damma on the ʿayn in the print, kept here; the form looks like the imperative of عَذَّلَ "to reproach" (expected عَذِّلْهُ), and the sense is uncertain.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا مَا سُورَةُ لَا أَعُودُ إِلَّا بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā mā sūratu lā aʿūdu illā bihi
sentences.l: And he said to her: What a form! I will not return except with him.
sentences.i: He said to her, "Never! I will not return except with him."

sentences.t: فَتَغَيَّرَ لَوْنُهَا وَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَا تَكُنْ كَثِيرَ الْكَلَامِ وَالْهَذَيَانِ فَإِنَّ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ مَا دَخَلَ إِلَيْنَا إِلَّا وَهُوَ وَاثِقٌ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ أَنَّهُ يَحْمِلُ عَلَى مِائَةِ فَارِسٍ وَحْدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-taghayyara lawnuhā wa-qālat lahu lā takun kathīra al-kalāmi wa-al-hadhayāni fa-inna hādhā al-rajula mā dakhala ilaynā illā wa-huwa wāthiqun min nafsihi annahu yaḥmilu ʿalā miʾati fārisin waḥdahu
sentences.l: And her colour changed, and she said to him: Do not be much of speech and of raving, for this man did not enter to us except while he is confident from himself that he charges upon a hundred horsemen, alone.
sentences.i: Her colour changed, and she said to him, "Do not talk so much and rave, for this man came in to us only because he is sure of himself, sure that he can charge a hundred horsemen alone."
sentences.n: وَاثِقٌ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ is "sure of himself". يَحْمِلُ عَلَى is "to charge at".

sentences.t: وَلَوْ قُلْتَ لَهُ أَنْتَ شَرْكَانُ بْنُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ يَقُولُ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: wa-law qulta lahu anta Sharkānu ibnu al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni yaqūlu naʿam
sentences.l: And if you said to him, You are Sharkān, son of the king ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, he would say, Yes.
sentences.i: If you said to him, "You are Sharkān, son of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān," he would answer, "Yes."

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ لَاأُمَكِّنُكُمْ أَنْ تَتَعَرَّضُوا لَهُ فَإِنْ تَعَرَّضْتُمْ لَهُ لَا يَعُودُ عَنْكُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قَتَلَ جَمِيعَ مَنْ كَانَ فِي هَذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin lā umakkinukum an tataʿarraḍū lahu fa-in taʿarraḍtum lahu lā yaʿūdu ʿankum illā an qatala jamīʿa man kāna fī hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: But I will not give-you-power that you offer-yourselves to him; and if you offer yourselves to him, he will not turn back from you unless he has killed all who were in this place.
sentences.i: But I will not let you molest him; and if you do, he will not turn back from you until he has killed every one in this place.
sentences.n: لَاأُمَكِّنُكُمْ is printed as one word. قَتَلَ is printed bare after إِلَّا أَنْ; we point it as a perfect ("has killed"), though classical usage would expect the subjunctive يَقْتُلَ.

sentences.t: وَهَاهُوَ عِنْدِي وَهَا أَنَا أُحْضِرُةُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَسَيْفُهُ وَخِفَّتُهُ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-hāhuwa ʿindī wa-hā anā uḥḍiruhu bayna aydīkum wa-sayfuhu wa-khiffatuhu maʿahu
sentences.l: And behold him, with me; and behold me, I bring him between your hands, and his sword and his lightness with him.
sentences.i: Here he is with me, and here I am bringing him before you, with his sword and his nimbleness about him.
sentences.n: أُحْضِرُةُ is printed with tāʾ marbūṭa for the pronoun -hu; we read it as -hu ("I bring him"). خِفَّتُهُ is read "his lightness", that is his agility; the word may be corrupt.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الْبِطْرِيقُ مَا سُورَةُ أَنَا إِذَا أَمِنْتُ مِنْ غَضَبِكِ لَمْ آمَنْ مِنْ غَضَبِ أَبِيكِ وَإِنِّي إِذَا رَأَبْتُهُ أُشِيرُ إِلَى الْبَطَارِقَةِ فَيَأْخُذُونَهُ أَسِيرًا وَنَمْضِي بِهِ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ حَقِيرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-biṭrīqu mā sūratu anā idhā amintu min ghaḍabiki lam āman min ghaḍabi abīki wa-innī idhā raʾabtuhu ushīru ilā al-baṭāriqati fa-yaʾkhudhūnahu asīran wa-namḍī bihi ilā al-maliki ḥaqīran
sentences.l: And the patrician said to her: What a form! If I am safe from your anger, I am not safe from the anger of your father; and I, when I see him, will point to the patricians, and they will take him captive, and we will go with him to the king, abased.
sentences.i: The patrician said to her, "Never! Though I may be safe from your anger, I am not safe from your father's. When I see him, I shall signal to the patricians; they will take him prisoner, and we shall carry him to the king in disgrace."
sentences.n: رَأَبْتُهُ is printed with bāʾ where the sense needs yāʾ (رَأَيْتُهُ, "I saw him"); we point it as printed. The verbs أُشِيرُ, فَيَأْخُذُونَهُ and نَمْضِي are indicative where classical usage would use the subjunctive after the fāʾ of consequence.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ مِنْهُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ قَالَتْ لَهُ لَا كَانَ هَذَا الْأَمْرُ فَإِنَّهُ عُنْوَانُ السَّفَهِ لِأَنَّ هَذَا رَجُلٌ وَاحِدٌ وَأَنْتُمْ مِائَةُ بِطْرِيقٍ فَإِذَا أَرَدْتُمْ مُصَادَمَتَهُ فَابْرُزُوا لَهُ وَاحِدًا بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ لِيَظْهَرَ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ مَنْ هُوَ أَبْطَلُ فِيكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat minhu hādhā al-kalāma qālat lahu lā kāna hādhā al-amru fa-innahu ʿunwānu al-safahi li-anna hādhā rajulun wāḥidun wa-antum miʾatu biṭrīqin fa-idhā aradtum muṣādamatahu fa-abruzū lahu wāḥidan baʿda wāḥidin li-yaẓhara ʿinda al-maliki man huwa abṭalu fīkum
sentences.l: And when she heard from him this speech, she said to him: May this matter not be! For it is the title of folly, because this is one man and you are a hundred patricians; so if you want to clash with him, come-out to him one after one, that it may appear at the king which of you is the more valiant.
sentences.i: When she heard this from him, she said, "Let that never be, for it is the very mark of folly. He is one man and you are a hundred patricians. If you want to fight him, come out to him one after another, so that the king may see which of you is the bravest."
sentences.n: لَا كَانَ هَذَا الْأَمْرُ is an optative "may this not be" with a past-tense verb. عُنْوَانُ السَّفَهِ is "the title (the very mark) of folly". أَبْطَلُ is read as an elative from بَطَل "hero" ("more valiant"); it could also be read as "more worthless" from بَاطِل, and the sense of a contest of champions favours "valiant".

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
